tagline: Valley farms, forested climbs and hot springs along an Oregon loop.
intro: The Grande Tour Route circles through farmland and mountain country, mixing gravel stretches with paved roads. Oregon’s transportation department presents this tour route as a journey through the valley’s mountains, farms and history, allowing four to five hours for 80 miles. The scenery changes from open country on Thief Valley Reservoir Road to pine and fir forest on the climb to Catherine Creek Summit. The valley return passes cherry orchards and mint fields beneath the Wallowa Mountains.

Travelers stopped here well before the tour route: Birnie Park in La Grande was a resting place for Oregon Trail emigrants before they crossed the Blue Mountains. Later, Hot Lake developed as a resort and hospital beside its thermal water. New highways changed its prospects: construction of U.S. 30 and Oregon 203 reduced passing traffic, and its owners converted the resort to a nursing home.

From La Grande, head south along the Blue Mountains to the Ladd Marsh viewpoint and past Hot Lake toward Union. The southern loop uses Oregon 237, Thief Valley Reservoir Road and Oregon 203, returning over Catherine Creek Summit to Union. Then Oregon 237 leads north to Cove; back roads follow the Grande Ronde River before the route crosses the valley and returns south on Mt. Glen Road to La Grande.

moments.title: Hot Lake
moments.text: Hot Lake supplied heat as well as the attraction for a resort and sanatorium. Its brick wing, completed in 1906, used the spring’s geothermal water for heating. A 1934 fire destroyed the wooden portion and bathhouse, while the eastern brick portion survived. After years as a nursing home and other businesses, the property was abandoned in 1991. Restoration began in 2003, followed by further renovations after an ownership change in 2020. The hotel and surrounding structures entered the National Register of Historic Places in 1979. The surviving wing has a Georgian-style U-shaped plan with a solarium facing the bluff.

moments.title: Medical Springs
moments.text: Medical Springs grew from a cabin and small bathhouse into a resort with a forty-room hotel. Dunham and Artemisia Wright homesteaded the place in the nineteenth century. The hotel added parlors and a ballroom, but fire destroyed it in 1917. A six-room replacement followed in 1918, a smaller successor to the original hotel. A spring-fed swimming pool was built in 1929. The community lies on Oregon 203 just outside Wallowa-Whitman National Forest. Dunham Wright continued living at the resort until 1942, dying shortly after his hundredth birthday, long after its first bathhouse was built.

moments.title: Cove
moments.text: Cove’s shortened name solved a postal problem. The post office opened as Forest Cove in 1863, but authorities dropped the first word in 1868 to avoid confusion with Forest Grove. The town was platted along Ruckles Road in the 1870s. Ascension Chapel, an Episcopal church built in 1869, is one of its landmarks. Mill Creek runs west through town from the Wallowa Mountains, while Oregon 237 passes along this eastern edge of the Grande Ronde Valley. Beyond Cove, the tour follows back roads past cherry orchards and mint fields at the base of the Wallowas.
